title: SBA 7(a) loans
metaDescription: SBA 7(a) loans are flexible, longer-term small-business loans partially guaranteed by the U.S. Small Business Administration. Fund44 matches you to lenders offering 7(a) financing for acquisitions, working capital, and growth.
summary: The SBA 7(a) page explains a flexible SBA-backed financing program and where it commonly fits for small-business borrowers.

hero.title: SBA 7(a) loans — flexible capital for growth.
hero.lead: The SBA 7(a) program is one of the most versatile small-business loan types. Fund44 helps you see whether it fits your goal and connects you with lenders that offer it.

quickAnswer.definition: is a small-business loan partially guaranteed by the U.S. Small Business Administration and issued by approved lenders. It can be used for working capital, business acquisition, equipment, refinancing, and more — typically with longer terms than conventional loans.

whoItFitsHeading: A single loan type for many needs

whoItFits.heading: When SBA 7(a) tends to fit
items: Acquiring an existing business or buying out a partner
Working capital to support operations and growth
Purchasing equipment or making leasehold improvements
Expansion into a new location or market

whenItMayNotFit.heading: When SBA 7(a) may not fit as well
items: Projects focused only on owner-occupied commercial real estate or heavy equipment may point more directly to SBA 504.
Borrowers who need a simpler flexible-cash-flow structure may prefer a line of credit or other working-capital option.

typicalDocuments.heading: Typical documents lenders may request
items: Supporting business-plan or acquisition materials when relevant

howFund44Fits.heading: How Fund44 fits
howFund44Fits.summary: Fund44 helps a borrower decide whether SBA 7(a) belongs in the mix and routes them toward providers that offer it.
bullets: Explains the program in plain language.
Places SBA 7(a) alongside other structured paths for comparison.
Keeps lender eligibility and final terms clearly outside Fund44's control.

eligibilityCards.description: The SBA program is for eligible for-profit businesses operating in the United States.

eligibilityCards.title: Ability to repay
eligibilityCards.description: Lenders review cash flow, revenue, and the business plan behind the request.

eligibilityCards.title: Owner background
eligibilityCards.description: Personal credit, experience, and a personal guarantee are commonly part of underwriting.

sectionDisclosureHtml: Fund44 is not a lender or the SBA. SBA 7(a) eligibility and terms are determined by SBA-approved lenders and SBA program rules, not by Fund44. Requirements and availability vary. This page is educational and is not a commitment to lend.

ctaBanner.heading: See if SBA 7(a) fits your plan.
ctaBanner.subheading: Answer a few questions and preview whether 7(a) — or another path — is a strong match.

commonQuestions.question: What can an SBA 7(a) loan be used for?
commonQuestions.answer: Common uses include business acquisition, working capital, equipment, leasehold improvements, expansion, and refinancing certain business debt. Allowed uses are defined by SBA program rules and the lender.

commonQuestions.question: How much can I borrow with an SBA 7(a) loan?
commonQuestions.answer: The SBA 7(a) program supports loans up to $5 million. The amount you may qualify for depends on your business profile and the lender’s underwriting.

commonQuestions.question: Is a personal guarantee required?
commonQuestions.answer: Lenders commonly require a personal guarantee from owners with significant ownership. Specific requirements are set by each lender and SBA rules.

commonQuestions.question: Does Fund44 issue SBA 7(a) loans?
commonQuestions.answer: No. Fund44 is a marketplace. It matches you with SBA-approved lenders in its network. Eligibility and terms are decided by those lenders.
